publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
title: FOMC forward rate guidance
instrument: Federal funds target or target range

definitions.tightening: The Committee explicitly described a prospective increase or further firming as its expected or specifically contemplated policy direction. Timing can be conditional.
definitions.easing: The Committee explicitly described a prospective reduction or further easing of the funds rate. A cut already announced is insufficient.
definitions.balanced: The Committee explicitly expected the current rate setting to persist, or explicitly presented competing rate directions on equal terms. A stable-rate signal can preserve a highly accommodative or restrictive stance.
definitions.unclear: The Committee did not identify a sufficiently explicit future rate direction or holding horizon. A warning on inflation or growth and a promise to respond to data alone fall here.

methodology: Selected date-stamped collective FOMC policy announcements. Each observation uses only the Committee’s publicly released statement on that date. Individual dissents, subsequent decisions and market pricing do not determine the classification.

State describes guidance after the announced decision. An explicit expectation to retain exceptionally low rates is a stable-rate signal. Anticipated removal of accommodation is a tightening signal even when the Committee says it can wait. Asset purchases, runoff and liquidity operations are identified separately where germane.

Holds without an explicit rate outlook are unclear. Economic risks described as balanced do not establish balanced rate guidance. A conditional restriction on when the Committee would consider an explicitly named cut or increase is identified in the evidence, without treating the condition as a promise.

Observations are selected, not interpolated. A comparison is available only when the immediately preceding federal funds policy decision in the publisher’s record was also verified here. A change involving unclear records a change in the specificity of communication and is not a directional score.

Action refers to the federal funds target, not the discount rate, portfolio or a dissenting vote. A zero rate change is a hold. The December 2008 switch from a point target to a range has no single comparable basis-point change.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: Even with productivity improving, policymakers thought spending might grow faster than potential supply and increase inflation pressure.
observations.analysis: The inflation-risk assessment accompanied a quarter-point rise. It did not specify another increase.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The Committee again judged demand growth excessive relative to supply and identified inflation as the predominant risk.
observations.analysis: Continuity with February applied to the diagnosis. The statement offered no path for the funds rate.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: Demand still exceeded rapid productivity-driven supply gains, and pressure on resources warranted a larger increase.
observations.analysis: A half-point move revealed the size of this adjustment. The remaining guidance concerned inflation risk.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: Demand appeared to be slowing toward potential, but tight resource use still left inflation as the main concern.
observations.analysis: The vote to pause after May did not include a commitment to keep rates steady.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: Moderating demand and productivity gains helped reconcile growth with supply. Tight labor markets still posed an inflation risk.
observations.analysis: The Committee retained an upside inflation assessment while taking no new rate action.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: Demand growth had moderated; unusually high resource utilization and energy costs still threatened price stability.
observations.analysis: An inflation warning survived the slowdown without becoming explicit guidance for the next meeting.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: A tight labor market and higher energy prices coexisted with softening spending and tighter financial conditions.
observations.analysis: The Committee still judged inflation the principal economic risk but gave no prospective funds-rate decision.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: Energy costs, deteriorating confidence and earnings shortfalls had shifted the predominant economic risk toward weakness.
observations.analysis: A genuine turn in the risk assessment occurred while the rate stayed put. The statement did not promise a cut.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: With sales and production weakening, the Committee cut between scheduled meetings and retained a downside economic-risk assessment.
observations.analysis: The Board of Governors separately signalled willingness to reduce its discount rate further. That was a different instrument and decision-maker.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: Eroding confidence and expensive energy reinforced weakness in demand. Inflation pressures remained contained.
observations.analysis: Repeated easing and a continued warning about growth still did not specify the next funds-rate move.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The attacks intensified uncertainty against an already weak backdrop for employment, output and investment.
observations.analysis: The release discussed liquidity provision during disrupted market functioning separately from the path of the policy rate.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: Economic activity remained soft, and underlying inflation could edge lower. The Committee continued to see greater risks of economic weakness.
observations.analysis: Economic risks and a current cut did not establish how much additional easing participants collectively expected.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: Signs of recovery had become more common, but the strength of final demand remained uncertain and downside economic risks persisted.
observations.analysis: Holding the rate as activity stabilized left the next decision open.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The Committee judged the risks to sustainable growth and price stability balanced as economic activity expanded.
observations.analysis: This is a balanced outlook for the mandate objectives. There was no comparable statement about the future rate.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: Weak financial markets and uncertainty had prolonged the slowdown in demand, leaving the economic risk tilted toward weakness.
observations.analysis: The return of downside economic risk did not produce a funds-rate commitment.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: After lowering the target, the Committee judged risks to its two economic objectives broadly balanced.
observations.analysis: The half-point cut changed the stance in effect. The risk assessment offered no path for a second adjustment.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The existing accommodative setting and productivity growth provided support, and risks to both objectives remained balanced.
observations.analysis: The description of current accommodation gave neither a duration nor a direction for the next change.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: Oil prices and geopolitical uncertainty were restraining spending and hiring; the Committee still viewed the overall economic risks as balanced.
observations.analysis: No explicit forward path for the rate followed from that assessment.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The Committee judged geopolitical uncertainty too great to characterize the balance of risks reliably and emphasized close monitoring.
observations.analysis: Withholding an economic risk assessment was itself informative, while the next funds-rate move remained open.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: Growth risks appeared balanced, but a further fall from already low inflation was more likely than an increase.
observations.analysis: The asymmetry concerned the distribution of inflation outcomes. The Committee did not explicitly guide toward a lower rate.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The Committee cut the target to 1%. Downside inflation risk still predominated despite broadly even growth risks.
observations.analysis: The statement described accommodation already in place without identifying another prospective move or a holding horizon.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: With inflation unusually low and substantial slack, the Committee expected accommodation could persist for an extended time.
observations.analysis: The new duration guidance favored keeping an accommodative setting. It did not signal an additional cut.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: Firmer spending had not prevented the labor market from weakening. The Committee again saw scope to maintain accommodation for an extended time.
observations.analysis: The low-rate holding horizon remained intact even as activity indicators improved.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: Spending was firming and employment appeared to be stabilizing, but subdued prices still supported a prolonged accommodative setting.
observations.analysis: The policy signal was persistence of the existing stance as the labor-market assessment improved.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The risk of declining inflation was closer to that of rising inflation. Low inflation and slack still justified maintaining accommodation for an extended time.
observations.analysis: A more symmetrical price outlook did not displace the explicit guidance about holding an accommodative rate.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The Committee said it could wait before withdrawing accommodation, placing an eventual withdrawal on the prospective policy path.
observations.analysis: The implied next direction was up, with timing deliberately left open and no increase at this meeting.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: Solid output growth and modest hiring gains left room for patience before removing accommodation.
observations.analysis: A preference to delay tightening is distinct from an intention to lower the rate.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: With inflation low but incoming readings firmer, the Committee described a gradual pace for withdrawing accommodation.
observations.analysis: The direction of the prospective move was explicit before the first increase occurred.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: Even after raising the target the Committee saw policy as accommodative and expected gradual further withdrawal, subject to the outlook.
observations.analysis: Both the current decision and the projected direction pointed upward, but the pace remained conditional.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The Committee still saw gradual removal of accommodation as appropriate despite balanced risks to growth and price stability.
observations.analysis: The economic balance-of-risks formula coexisted with a directional policy signal.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: After raising the target to 4.25%, the Committee expected some further gradual tightening to keep economic risks in balance.
observations.analysis: The statement named a prospective direction while allowing the data to alter it.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: After lifting the rate to 5.25%, the Committee explicitly contemplated additional firming, with its timing and extent dependent on growth and inflation.
observations.analysis: This was a conditional upside option, weaker than a commitment to continue increasing at a set pace.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The Committee kept 5.25% as growth moderated, but it still identified additional firming as the potential next adjustment.
observations.analysis: A pause in the realized hiking cycle coexisted with a conditional tightening bias.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The Committee still saw some inflation risk and singled out possible further firming, conditional on the outlook.
observations.analysis: Several months at the same rate had not produced a promise of stable rates.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: Although the Committee highlighted the danger that inflation might not moderate, its policy paragraph made future adjustments dependent on growth and inflation without specifying their direction.
observations.analysis: An asymmetric concern about inflation did not amount to explicit guidance for a further increase.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The half-point cut was intended to cushion the economy against tightening credit. The Committee would reassess financial conditions and respond as needed.
observations.analysis: Its explanation of the cut did not identify the next funds-rate adjustment.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: Following another cut, the Committee saw the risks of higher inflation and weaker growth as roughly offsetting and offered a contingent response to subsequent developments.
observations.analysis: Balanced economic risks did not establish either a future hold or equal probabilities of hikes and cuts.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: Deteriorating market conditions and housing activity prompted a quarter-point cut. Future action remained contingent on the outlook.
observations.analysis: The easing delivered at this meeting was clearer than the rate path that would follow.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: An intermeeting cut addressed a deteriorating outlook and tighter credit. The Committee remained ready to respond promptly to downside growth risks.
observations.analysis: The readiness to act identified the risk being managed without specifying a subsequent funds-rate move.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The rate was cut to 3% amid financial stress and tighter credit. Downside risks remained after earlier policy actions.
observations.analysis: The pledge to respond promptly to those risks was not an explicit promise of another rate cut.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The Committee cut to 2.25% as the outlook weakened, while acknowledging that the inflation outlook had also become more uncertain.
observations.analysis: The future response addressed both objectives and did not identify a particular funds-rate direction.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: A quarter-point reduction brought the rate to 2%. The Committee noted both subdued spending and higher commodity prices and inflation expectations.
observations.analysis: Planned monitoring and a readiness to respond did not specify the next rate decision.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The target remained 2%. Downside growth risks appeared somewhat smaller while upside risks to inflation and expectations had increased.
observations.analysis: The shift in the risk assessment was material without constituting a stated intention to raise rates.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The Committee held at 2% and remained concerned about both financial stress and uncertainty around inflation.
observations.analysis: Concern about prices and a current hold left future rate policy open.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: At the 2% hold, downside growth risks and upside inflation risks were both significant. The Committee said it would monitor financial developments and act as needed.
observations.analysis: This two-sided description concerned the economy. No future rate direction was stated.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: In the coordinated response, the US Committee cut to 1.5%. Deteriorating activity and falling commodity prices had reduced upside inflation risks.
observations.analysis: The US paragraph linked the move to the crisis without committing to the direction of a subsequent decision.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The Committee reduced the target to 1% and saw remaining downside growth risks even after earlier policy and liquidity measures.
observations.analysis: Its stated willingness to respond did not specify an additional reduction.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The Committee replaced the 1% point target with a 0–0.25% range and expected economic weakness to justify very low rates for some time.
observations.analysis: The prospective rate message concerned persistence at very low levels. Introducing a range precludes a unique basis-point change.
observations.balanceSheet: The Fed planned substantial agency debt and mortgage-security purchases and was evaluating longer-term Treasury purchases.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The Committee maintained the 0–0.25% range and expected exceptionally low rates to remain warranted for a period of time.
observations.analysis: It distinguished the stable short-rate outlook from scope to supply further support through its portfolio.
observations.balanceSheet: Agency purchases were under way. The Fed stood ready to expand them and was prepared to purchase longer-term Treasury securities if warranted.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The Committee maintained 0–0.25% and explicitly expected exceptionally low rates to be needed for a prolonged period.
observations.analysis: The clearer duration signal came with considerable new accommodation through a different instrument.
observations.balanceSheet: Authorized purchases included up to $750 billion more agency mortgage-backed securities, $100 billion more agency debt and $300 billion in longer-term Treasuries.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: Slack, subdued inflation and stable expectations were expected to justify an extended period of exceptionally low rates.
observations.analysis: Rate guidance concerned staying low while reinvestment policy sought to prevent passive balance-sheet contraction.
observations.balanceSheet: Principal received from agency debt and agency mortgage-backed securities would be reinvested in longer-term Treasuries to maintain the level of securities holdings.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The Committee retained its extended low-rate horizon and indicated readiness to offer additional accommodation if required.
observations.analysis: The statement did not identify another funds-rate reduction as the vehicle for that potential support.
observations.balanceSheet: The Committee retained its existing reinvestment policy.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The 0–0.25% range and extended low-rate guidance remained. The additional easing came through securities purchases.
observations.analysis: A stable rate outlook is compatible with active easing through the quantity and maturity of assets held.
observations.balanceSheet: The Committee intended to purchase another $600 billion of longer-term Treasuries by the end of 2011 Q2, about $75 billion per month.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The Committee placed a date on its low-rate outlook, expecting exceptionally low rates to remain warranted at least through mid-2013.
observations.analysis: The dated expectation gave more precise holding guidance without indicating an additional rate cut.
observations.balanceSheet: Existing reinvestment policy was maintained.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The Committee reaffirmed its expectation of very low rates at least through mid-2013 as it recognized downside risks to activity.
observations.analysis: Unchanged date guidance coexisted with a change in the maturity structure of the portfolio.
observations.balanceSheet: It intended to buy $400 billion of longer-dated Treasuries and sell an equal amount of shorter-dated holdings by the end of June 2012.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The Committee expected exceptionally low rates at least through mid-2015 and accommodation to continue even after activity strengthened.
observations.analysis: The horizon concerned the funds rate. A separate, labor-market-contingent commitment applied to additional purchases.
observations.balanceSheet: Agency mortgage purchases began at $40 billion per month, with further accommodation envisaged if labor-market prospects failed to improve substantially.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The low rate was expected to persist while unemployment exceeded 6.5%, the one-to-two-year inflation projection did not exceed 2.5% and longer-run expectations stayed anchored.
observations.analysis: Those conditions were thresholds for reassessment, not an automatic hiking trigger.
observations.balanceSheet: The statement paired $40 billion in monthly agency mortgage purchases with an initial $45 billion per month of longer-term Treasury purchases.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The Committee expected the range to stay near zero well after unemployment fell below 6.5%, particularly if projected inflation remained below target.
observations.analysis: Extending the possible holding period separated rate policy from the simultaneously announced slowing of asset purchases.
observations.balanceSheet: From January, the pace would fall to $35 billion monthly for agency mortgage securities and $40 billion for longer-term Treasuries. Both holdings would still grow.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The Committee anticipated retaining the near-zero range for a considerable time after the asset purchase program ended, especially with below-target projected inflation and anchored expectations.
observations.analysis: Ending net purchases did not immediately end the expected rate hold.
observations.balanceSheet: Net asset purchases ended this month. Reinvestment and Treasury rollovers continued.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The Committee judged it could wait before beginning policy normalization and explicitly regarded this as consistent with its earlier low-rate holding guidance.
observations.analysis: Normalization identified the eventual direction. The Committee emphasized patience and continuity rather than imminent liftoff.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The first move raised the range to 0.25–0.50%, and policymakers expected economic conditions to justify only gradual additional rate increases.
observations.analysis: The anticipated direction was explicit while the pace depended on economic conditions.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: After a quarter-point increase, the Committee expected only gradual further rate rises and a rate below its longer-run level for a time.
observations.analysis: The longer-run comparison described how far normalization might proceed, rather than a timetable.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The rate stayed at 1.00–1.25%. The Committee still expected the economy to justify a gradual increase in the funds rate.
observations.analysis: Rate guidance remained upward even at a meeting whose immediate policy change concerned the portfolio.
observations.balanceSheet: The Committee scheduled the start of balance-sheet normalization for October.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: After raising the range to 2.25–2.50%, the Committee judged that some further gradual increases would be consistent with continued expansion and near-target inflation.
observations.analysis: The expectation was for additional increases conditional on the outlook, without specifying a number or terminal rate.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The Committee said it would be patient in deciding which future rate adjustments were appropriate, citing global developments and muted inflation.
observations.analysis: Unlike its previous statement, it no longer identified increases as the expected direction. Patience applied to deciding what to do.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: Increased uncertainty and subdued inflation led the Committee to emphasize readiness to act to sustain the expansion. It retained the current range.
observations.analysis: That reaction to uncertain conditions did not name a prospective cut; the dissent for one did not establish the majority’s guidance.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The quarter-point reduction responded to global developments and muted inflation. Subsequent policy was left conditional on incoming information.
observations.analysis: A realized cut did not establish an explicit commitment to repeat it.
observations.balanceSheet: The Committee brought forward the end of the reduction in securities holdings to August, two months earlier than previously indicated.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The Committee cut to 1.50–1.75% and said it would evaluate the appropriate future path in light of new information.
observations.analysis: The statement specified the decision taken but gave neither a holding horizon nor a prospective rate direction.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The coronavirus posed evolving risks to activity. The Committee made an intermeeting half-point cut and said it would use its tools to support the economy.
observations.analysis: Its readiness to use tools did not specify a second funds-rate cut.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The Committee cut to 0–0.25% and expected to maintain this range until it was confident the economy had weathered the shock and was on course for its objectives.
observations.analysis: The immediate change was a full percentage point of easing. The prospective rate guidance was an outcome-dependent hold.
observations.balanceSheet: It planned at least $500 billion of additional Treasury holdings and at least $200 billion of additional agency mortgage-security holdings to support market functioning.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The Committee retained the near-zero range and expected it to last until the economy had weathered the public-health shock and was on track toward its objectives.
observations.analysis: This was a condition for maintaining the range, expressed during a sharp decline in employment and activity.
observations.balanceSheet: Treasury, agency residential and agency commercial mortgage securities would be purchased in amounts needed for orderly markets.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The Committee expected to retain the near-zero range until maximum-employment conditions were reached and inflation had reached 2% and was on track to run moderately above it for a time.
observations.analysis: The conditions tied the rate to observed progress and the prospective inflation path. An overshoot objective was not a further rate cut.
observations.balanceSheet: Treasury and agency mortgage holdings would continue to increase at least at the current pace over coming months.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The near-zero range was still expected to last until maximum-employment conditions and the stated inflation conditions were achieved.
observations.analysis: Tapering net purchases was compatible with continued conditional low-rate guidance.
observations.balanceSheet: Monthly additions to holdings would slow by $10 billion for Treasuries and $5 billion for agency mortgage securities.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: With inflation already above 2% for a time, the Committee now tied maintaining the current rate range to reaching maximum-employment conditions.
observations.analysis: The remaining hurdle narrowed without an explicit instruction that the next meeting would deliver a hike.
observations.balanceSheet: The Committee accelerated the taper, reducing monthly additions by $20 billion for Treasuries and $10 billion for agency mortgage securities.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: Elevated inflation and a strong labor market led the Committee to explicitly anticipate that an increase in the range would soon be appropriate.
observations.analysis: The change in forward guidance arrived before liftoff. The target remained 0–0.25%.
observations.balanceSheet: The Committee planned to finish net asset purchases in early March.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: Liftoff took the range to 0.25–0.50%, and the Committee anticipated a continuing series of appropriate increases.
observations.analysis: The decision began to deliver the upward direction signalled at the January meeting.
observations.balanceSheet: The Committee expected to begin reducing its holdings at a future meeting.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The Committee raised the range to 0.75–1.00% and continued to expect further increases, given high inflation and a strong labor market.
observations.analysis: The larger current step did not specify the size of later steps.
observations.balanceSheet: Runoff of Treasury, agency debt and agency mortgage holdings would start on June 1.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The Committee raised the range to 1.50–1.75% and still explicitly anticipated further increases as inflation remained elevated.
observations.analysis: The larger move and the forward direction are separate observations; no sequence of three-quarter-point increases was promised.
observations.balanceSheet: Runoff would continue under the previously announced plan.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The rate rose to 2.25–2.50%. Despite softer spending and production indicators, the Committee still anticipated further increases.
observations.analysis: The change in activity language did not reverse the stated direction of rate guidance.
observations.balanceSheet: Securities holdings would continue to decline under the plan announced in May.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The Committee raised the range to 3.00–3.25% and retained its expectation of further increases amid elevated inflation and a strong labor market.
observations.analysis: The policy signal still named an upward path without fixing the size of its next step.
observations.balanceSheet: Portfolio runoff continued.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The Committee raised the target and expected more increases to achieve sufficient restraint. It explicitly introduced cumulative tightening and policy lags into decisions about pace.
observations.analysis: Acknowledging delayed transmission qualified the speed of subsequent hikes, without reversing their expected direction.
observations.balanceSheet: Portfolio runoff continued.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The half-point increase slowed the realized pace. Further increases were still expected to bring policy to a sufficiently restrictive setting.
observations.analysis: The statement distinguished how rapidly the rate would rise from the need for additional restraint.
observations.balanceSheet: Portfolio runoff continued.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The Committee raised the range by a quarter point and still anticipated further increases. It focused on their extent in light of previous tightening and transmission lags.
observations.analysis: A smaller step and a focus on the amount remaining did not remove the explicit upward direction.
observations.balanceSheet: Portfolio runoff continued.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: Following a quarter-point increase, the Committee judged further firming might be needed and acknowledged tighter credit conditions following banking strains.
observations.analysis: The reference to possible additional tightening was less definite than February’s continuing series of increases.
observations.balanceSheet: Portfolio runoff continued.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: Following the increase to 5.00–5.25%, the Committee would assess whether more firming was warranted, accounting for earlier tightening, lags and financial developments.
observations.analysis: The only named prospective directional adjustment remained tightening, now an option rather than an expectation.
observations.balanceSheet: Portfolio runoff continued.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: Holding at 5.00–5.25% bought time to assess additional information. The Committee still explicitly discussed the possible extent of further firming.
observations.analysis: A meeting-level pause did not remove the conditional upside option from rate guidance.
observations.balanceSheet: Portfolio runoff continued.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The Committee raised the range to 5.25–5.50% and retained its conditional language about whether additional firming would be warranted.
observations.analysis: The quarter-point move implemented one increase without resolving the need for another.
observations.balanceSheet: Portfolio runoff continued.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The Committee held the range and continued to frame the next directional option as possible additional firming, subject to cumulative tightening and lags.
observations.analysis: A steady current rate and an explicit conditional upside option remained compatible.
observations.balanceSheet: Portfolio runoff continued.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The Committee judged that tighter financial and credit conditions could weigh on activity, while still specifically considering possible further firming.
observations.analysis: A less certain need for an increase did not introduce an explicit easing option.
observations.balanceSheet: Portfolio runoff continued.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The Committee added a qualifier when discussing whether any further firming might be appropriate. It still named that conditional upside option while leaving the rate unchanged.
observations.analysis: The explicitness of an upside option is weaker evidence than a forecast of another hike. No numerical probability is implied.
observations.balanceSheet: Portfolio runoff continued.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The Committee kept 5.25–5.50%, dropped its description of potential further firming and identified greater confidence in lasting disinflation as a condition for reducing the rate.
observations.analysis: Cuts became the specifically discussed directional option. The Committee explicitly said it did not yet expect a cut to be appropriate before that condition was met.
observations.balanceSheet: Portfolio runoff continued.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The Committee again made a possible reduction conditional on greater confidence that inflation would return sustainably to 2%.
observations.analysis: The hurdle applied to cutting. Holding the range at this meeting did not give a date for easing.
observations.balanceSheet: Portfolio runoff continued.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: Recent inflation progress had stalled. The Committee kept its condition that greater confidence in sustained disinflation was necessary before reducing the rate.
observations.analysis: A deterioration in the evidence for satisfying the hurdle delayed the case for cuts without introducing explicit hike guidance.
observations.balanceSheet: The monthly Treasury redemption cap would drop from $60 billion to $25 billion in June.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The Committee saw modest renewed progress on inflation and still required greater confidence in sustained disinflation before a reduction was appropriate.
observations.analysis: Improved inflation news changed the evidence relevant to the condition, while the formal cut threshold remained.
observations.balanceSheet: Portfolio runoff continued.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The Committee retained the disinflation-confidence hurdle for reducing the rate, while noting risks to both parts of its mandate.
observations.analysis: The communication identified the conditional direction under consideration without fixing the timing or size of a reduction.
observations.balanceSheet: Portfolio runoff continued.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The Committee cut the range by half a percentage point. Its prospective language now addressed possible further adjustments in generic, data-dependent terms.
observations.analysis: The conditional cut discussed earlier had occurred. The adopted statement did not explicitly specify the direction of the adjustment after it.
observations.balanceSheet: Portfolio runoff continued.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The Committee lowered the range to 4.50–4.75% and conditioned further adjustments on the outlook, risks and incoming data.
observations.analysis: The quarter-point cut was an action, while the Committee kept its prospective wording direction-neutral.
observations.balanceSheet: Portfolio runoff continued.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The Committee reduced the range to 4.25–4.50% and placed the extent and timing of subsequent adjustments under review.
observations.analysis: The target had moved down, but the Committee did not specifically call for another reduction in its forward language.
observations.balanceSheet: Portfolio runoff continued.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The Committee lowered the target to 3.75–4.00% and said further adjustments would depend on incoming evidence and risks.
observations.analysis: The wording allowed more action but did not specify the direction of the next move.
observations.balanceSheet: The Committee separately set December 1 as the end date for reducing its aggregate securities holdings.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The Committee cut to 3.50–3.75% and left the extent and timing of subsequent changes dependent on the data and outlook.
observations.analysis: An actual cut and flexibility about what follows are distinct signals.
observations.balanceSheet: Shorter-dated Treasury purchases were authorized as needed to maintain ample reserves. The statement identified a reserve-management objective.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: At 3.50–3.75%, the Committee left the timing and extent of further adjustments conditional on incoming information, the outlook and risks.
observations.analysis: Stabilization in unemployment and still-elevated inflation appeared in the diagnosis without an explicit prospective rate direction.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The Committee again made further rate adjustments conditional. It described the US implications of Middle East developments as uncertain and acknowledged risks to both objectives.
observations.analysis: Uncertainty over the shock did not translate into an explicit preference to ease, tighten or remain at this level for a stated horizon.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The adopted policy paragraph retained the generic reference to further adjustments even as higher global energy prices contributed to elevated inflation.
observations.analysis: Three voters who supported the hold explicitly objected to what they read as an easing bias. The majority’s paragraph did not itself name cuts as the next direction.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The unanimous statement held the range, identified sectoral supply shocks and reaffirmed the price-stability objective without describing the next funds-rate move.
observations.analysis: The commitment concerned the inflation outcome, leaving both the instrument path and timing unspecified.
observations.balanceSheet: The Committee reaffirmed an ample-reserves operating policy.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The majority maintained the range and again emphasized above-goal inflation and supply shocks without stating an expected rate change.
observations.analysis: Three dissents favored an immediate quarter-point increase. They describe individual votes on this decision, not forward guidance from the majority.
observations.balanceSheet: The statement retained the ample-reserves policy.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The unanimous quarter-point increase took the range to 3.75–4.00%. The Committee said this action should speed the return to target and offered no subsequent move.
observations.analysis: A stronger anti-inflation action occurred without explicit guidance about another hike.
observations.balanceSheet: The statement retained the ample-reserves policy.

observations.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
observations.title: FOMC monetary policy statement
observations.evidence: The Committee maintained 3.75–4.00% and said further information would help determine the appropriate stance. Activity was strong and inflation elevated.
observations.analysis: Two members preferred an immediate hike. The majority neither adopted that proposal nor set a future rate direction.
observations.balanceSheet: The statement retained the ample-reserves policy.
